translations.idiomatic: A local bully held leverage over every official who came through, and successive governors and magistrates all feared him.

sentences.zh: 文同下車，聞其名而數之。

translations.literal: When Wentong took up his post he heard the man's name and had him counted and punished.
translations.idiomatic: When Wentong took office he heard the man's name and had him arrested.

sentences.zh: 因令剡木為大橛，埋之於庭，出尺餘，四面各埋小橛，令其人踣心於木橛上，縛四支於小橛，以棒打其背，應時潰爛。

translations.literal: He then ordered wood carved into a great stake buried in the courtyard with more than a foot exposed; on four sides smaller stakes were buried; the man was made to lie chest-down on the great stake with his four limbs bound to the small stakes, and was beaten on the back with clubs until his flesh instantly burst and rotted.
translations.idiomatic: He had a large wooden stake carved and buried in the courtyard with a foot exposed, with smaller stakes on four sides. The man was laid chest-down on the large stake with limbs bound to the smaller ones and beaten on the back until his flesh burst apart.

sentences.zh: 郡中大駭，吏人懾氣。

translations.literal: The whole commandery was greatly terrified; officials and people were cowed into submission.
translations.idiomatic: The whole commandery was terrified, and officials and commoners alike submitted in fear.

sentences.zh: 及帝征遼東，令文同巡察河北諸郡，文同見沙門齋戒菜食者，以為妖妄，皆收系之。

translations.literal: When the emperor campaigned in Liaodong he ordered Wentong to inspect the commanderies of Hebei; Wentong saw monks observing fasts and eating vegetables and considered them deluded and false, arresting and imprisoning them all.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor campaigned in Liaodong, Wentong was ordered to inspect the Hebei commanderies. He arrested all monks he found fasting and eating vegetables, deeming them deluded.

sentences.zh: 北至河間，召郡官人。

translations.literal: Going north to Hejian he summoned the commandery officials.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching Hejian in the north, he summoned the commandery officials.

sentences.zh: 小有遲違者，輒覆面於地而捶殺之。

translations.literal: Whoever was slightly tardy or disobedient was forthwith laid face-down on the ground and beaten to death.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone who was slightly tardy was laid face-down and beaten to death.

sentences.zh: 求沙門相聚講論及長老共為佛會者數百人，文同以為聚結惑眾，盡斬之。

translations.literal: He found several hundred monks gathered to discuss doctrine and elders jointly holding Buddhist assemblies; Wentong considered this gathering to delude the masses and beheaded them all.
translations.idiomatic: He found several hundred monks gathered for doctrinal discussion and Buddhist assemblies. Wentong deemed this sedition and beheaded them all.

sentences.zh: 又悉裸僧尼，驗有淫狀非童男女者數千人，復將殺之。

translations.literal: He also stripped all monks and nuns bare; examining them, several thousand who showed signs of licentiousness and were not celibate youths were again about to be killed.
translations.idiomatic: He also stripped all monks and nuns and examined them. Finding several thousand who were not celibate, he prepared to execute them as well.

sentences.zh: 郡中士女，號哭於路，諸郡驚駭，各奏其事。

translations.literal: Men and women of the commandery wailed along the roads; the various commanderies were alarmed and terrified, each memorializing the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Men and women of the commandery wailed in the streets. The neighboring commanderies were horrified and each memorialized the emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝聞大怒，遣使者違奚善意馳鎖之，斬於河間，以謝百姓。

translations.literal: The emperor heard and was greatly enraged; he sent an envoy, Wei Xishanyi, by rapid post to chain him, and he was beheaded at Hejian to appease the people.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was enraged and sent the envoy Wei Xishanyi to seize him. Wentong was beheaded at Hejian to appease the people.

sentences.zh: 仇人剖其棺，臠其肉啖之，斯須咸盡。

translations.literal: His enemies opened his coffin, sliced his flesh, and ate it—in an instant it was all gone.
translations.idiomatic: His enemies opened his coffin, cut his flesh into strips, and ate it until nothing remained.

translations.literal: Commentary
translations.idiomatic: Commentary

sentences.zh: 論曰：士之立名，其途不一，或以循良進，或以嚴酷顯。

translations.literal: The commentary says: For gentlemen to establish a name, the paths are not one—they may advance through dutiful goodness, or become prominent through severity and cruelty.
translations.idiomatic: The commentary says: Gentlemen establish their reputations by different paths—some through dutiful governance, others through harsh severity.

sentences.zh: 故寬猛相資，德刑互設。

translations.literal: Therefore leniency and severity support one another; virtue and punishment are set in turn.
translations.idiomatic: Leniency and severity must complement each other; moral teaching and punishment must work together.

sentences.zh: 然不嚴而化，君子所先。

translations.literal: Yet to transform without severity is what gentlemen put first.
translations.idiomatic: Yet gentlemen prefer transformation without harshness.

sentences.zh: 于洛侯等為惡不同，同歸於酷，肆其毒螫，多行殘忍。

translations.literal: Yu Luohou and the others committed different evils but alike ended in cruelty, unleashing their poisonous stings and frequently acting with savage cruelty.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Luohou and the others committed different crimes, yet all alike ended in cruelty, unleashing their venom and acting with savage brutality.

sentences.zh: 賤人肌膚，同諸木石；

translations.literal: They despised human flesh as no more than wood and stone;
translations.idiomatic: They treated human flesh as no more than wood and stone;

sentences.zh: 輕人性命，甚於芻狗。

translations.literal: they held human life lighter than straw dogs.
translations.idiomatic: they valued human life less than straw dogs.

sentences.zh: 長惡不悛，鮮有不及。

translations.literal: Persisting in evil without repentance, few failed to meet their downfall.
translations.idiomatic: Persisting in evil without repentance, few escaped their downfall.

sentences.zh: 故或身嬰罪戮，或憂恚俱殞，異術皆斃，各其宜焉。

translations.literal: Therefore some personally suffered punishment and execution, others perished together with grief and rage—different fates, all ending in death, each as was fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Some were executed for their crimes, others died of grief and rage—different ends, all meeting death as each deserved.

sentences.zh: 凡百君子，以為有天道矣。

translations.literal: All gentlemen of principle took this as evidence that Heaven's Way exists.
translations.idiomatic: All men of principle took this as proof that Heaven's justice endures.
